name: Morou-Ngou
body:
MOROU-NGOU
CR 8

This huge spotted cat has shaggy light brown fur, dappled with spots and a long, thick tail, while oversized fangs flank its jaws.

XP 4,800
NE Huge magical beast
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 10, flat-footed 14 (+2 Dex, +6 natural, -2 size)
hp 85 (9d10+36)
Fort +10, Ref +8, Will +4

OFFENSE

Speed 50 ft., swim 25 ft.
Melee 2 claws +15 (2d8+7/19-20), bite +14 (2d8+7 plus trip)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks capsize, pounce, roar

STATISTICS

Str 24, Dex 15, Con 18, Int 7, Wis 12, Cha 14
Base Atk +9; CMB +18; CMD 36 (40 vs. trip)
Feats Improved Critical (claw), Improved Initiative, Outflank, Precise Strike, Weapon Focus (claw)
Skills Acrobatics +7 (+15 to jump), Climb +11, Perception +8, Survival +5, Swim +20

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Capsize (Ex)

A morou-ngou can overturn a boat of its size or Smaller by ramming it as a charge attack and making a CMB check. The DC of this check is 25 or the result of the boat captain’s Profession (sailor) check, whichever is higher.

Roar (Ex)

A morou-ngou can use its dreadful roar as a standard action to cause creatures within 30 feet to become frightened for 1d4 rounds. It can roar as a swift action to cause creatures in a 15-foot cone to become frightened for 1 round. A successful DC 16 Will save negates either effect, but creatures failing their save by 5 or more are cowering instead of frightened. A creature that successfully saves is immune to that morou-ngou’s roar for 1 hour.

This is a mind-affecting fear effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm plains and marshes
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure none

These aquatic great cats are apex predators who post a major threat to beasts and people traversing large rivers. They’re recognizable by their brownish fur, which is either striped or dappled with blue and white spots like those of a leopard.

The morou-ngou’s head is closer to that of a civet than a lion, with glowing eyes and impressive canines. Its tracks resemble those of a leopard, though considerably larger, and its general body shape is similar to that of an oversized great cat. It is about the size of an elephant, and it is known to feed on such creatures, as well as on hippos.

Morou-ngou hunt in pairs, with one cat driving their target in the water while the other incapacitates their prey.

They have been known to capsize canoes and feast on people traveling the river. They often kill prey even when they aren’t hungry, lending credence to the notion that they possess a form of malevolent cunning significantly greater than that of most beasts.

The roar of a morou-ngou resembles a rushing wind. It is more potent than that of other great cats, and indeed, the sound can paralyze those who are too close to the morou-ngou.
